summary: error and loaded state never reset when src prop changes, causing stale fallback on new valid URL
failure_scenario: If the same media item's poster_url changes (e.g., data recache or TMDB poster update), a previously errored image permanently shows the letter-initial placeholder even though the new URL is valid. The loaded state also stays true, suppressing the loading shimmer for the new image.

summary: 429 retry fetch has no timeout protection — clearTimeout runs before retry, no new timeout is set
failure_scenario: After a 429 response, clearTimeout(timeout) at line 61 cancels the 4s timeout. The retry fetch at line 64 reuses the same controller.signal (never aborted) with no new timeout. If TMDB remains slow or the network stalls, the retry hangs indefinitely, blocking the server function and preventing fallback data from being served.

summary: Fallback path uses wrapperClassName || className for the outer div, but success path ignores className on the wrapper, causing layout mismatch when wrapperClassName is omitted
failure_scenario: A caller that omits wrapperClassName and passes only className (e.g., className="absolute inset-0 h-full w-full") gets correct absolute positioning in the fallback/error state, but the success path wrapper collapses to 0 height (only "relative overflow-hidden" with no explicit dimensions) while the img is absolutely positioned — the image vanishes.

summary: Error message always says '(rate limited)' even when retry returns a non-429 status
failure_scenario: After a 429 response, the retry returns 401 (revoked token) or 500 (server error). The error reads 'TMDB 401 (rate limited)' or 'TMDB 500 (rate limited)', misdirecting debugging toward rate-limit issues when the real cause is authentication or server error.

summary: AniList GraphQL fetch in cacheMedia lacks AbortController/timeout, inconsistent with new TMDB timeout pattern
failure_scenario: If the AniList API hangs or is unreachable, the cacheMedia server function can stall for the full serverless platform timeout (10-30s), blocking the user from adding anime to their library. The TMDB path was just hardened with a 4s timeout, but the AniList path was not updated to match.

summary: Falsy-zero check: a.averageScore ? a.averageScore / 10 : null treats 0 as falsy, producing null instead of 0
failure_scenario: AniList API returns averageScore of 0 (valid 0-100 scale, maps to 0.0/10). The ternary treats 0 as falsy, so vote_average becomes null instead of 0, silently erasing a legitimate zero score from the user's display.

summary: 4-second TMDB timeout applied uniformly to all endpoints including slow ones like trending/all/week
failure_scenario: TMDB's /trending/all/week endpoint commonly takes 4-6 seconds under normal conditions. The 4s timeout fires, and callers like trending() and discover() fall back to static placeholder data (Inception, Breaking Bad, etc.) instead of real trending content. The searchAll handler falls back to stale cached data. getDetails has no fallback and throws an error page.

summary: Race condition: clearTimeout(timeout) runs after fetch resolves but timeout callback may have already fired, leaving controller aborted for retry
failure_scenario: Under heavy CPU load, the setTimeout callback (controller.abort()) fires between the fetch promise resolution and the clearTimeout(timeout) execution. The controller signal becomes permanently aborted. The 429 check still passes, but the retry fetch at line 64 immediately rejects with AbortError because the signal is already in aborted state, causing an unnecessary fallback.

summary: Five raw tags in profile.tsx (lines 109, 214, 240, 263, 295) lack SafeImage's error/loading handling
failure_scenario: When poster/avatar URLs return 404 (e.g., stale TMDB data or deleted avatar), the profile page shows broken-image icons instead of SafeImage's graceful letter-initial fallback with loading shimmer. This affects the avatar, top-rated posters, favorites posters, recently-added posters, and follower avatars.

summary: loading='lazy' is hardcoded on the element with no prop to override for above-fold or hero images
failure_scenario: Future callers using SafeImage for LCP-critical images (hero banners, above-the-fold posters) cannot opt into loading='eager'. The hardcoded lazy loading delays image visibility and harms Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) scores. Both removed callers explicitly used loading='lazy', but the component should expose this as a prop.
